title: I Enforced the Mini-Golf Rain-Check Date on the Desk That Dated It Wrong

parts.text: I redeemed a rain check at 2:14 p.m. on the date stamped in red. The desk had rewritten the date in pen to yesterday. The rain-check card the owner posted said: RED STAMP GOVERNS. NO PEN EDITS. I was thirty, date-night putter, holding the original. Desk Riley said, "Pen is weather." I pointed at the card. They shrugged. "Weather moves." I photographed the red stamp, the pen, and the card. Then I asked the owner kiosk to scan the barcode under the stamp. At 2:19 the owner asked why Riley's pen was on a rain-check alter ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner can see yesterday in pen over a red stamp that says today.

social.video_title: The desk penned yesterday on today's rain check — Part 1/2
social.description: Red stamp, a pen edit, and a card that bans both. I scanned the barcode. Would you have putted in the rain originally?

parts.text: Riley called it a smear until the barcode matched today. I printed the ticket, the card, and the photo. We putted. Riley told the windmill the card was always about optics. Optics is a word desks use when a barcode exists. Rain-check policy now has a second line: PEN IS NOT WEATHER. I keep the stub. Riley stamps only. The eighteenth hole finally counts the red.

social.video_title: Pen is not weather on a rain check — Part 2/2
social.description: Alter ticket, a real round, and a second line on the card. Was weather ever a rewrite?
